inventory.reportSummary: Audited TaskBoard (http://127.0.0.1:9902/) at iPhone 15 size (393×852) with a desktop cross-check. The board itself renders and core interactions work: the kanban shows 4 columns with seeded tasks, the Add Task modal opens, a task with a title is created successfully, Cancel dismisses, and clicking a task card advances it to the next column. However, navigation is fundamentally broken: My Tasks, Team, Reports, and Sign In routes all render the Project Board regardless of whether the link is clicked or the URL is loaded directly, so 4 of 5 destinations (including authentication) are unreachable. On mobile the header also overflows, pushing the Sign In link entirely off-screen. Add Task gives no feedback on empty submit, and all task changes are lost on reload (in-memory state only). No console errors or failed network requests were observed. Verdict: pass with issues — the board flow functions, but routing, mobile navigation access, validation feedback, and persistence need fixing before release.

intelligence.rootCause: The New Task form's submit handler almost certainly contains a guard clause (e.g. `if (!title.trim()) return;`) that aborts silently when the title is empty, without setting any error state or rendering a validation message. The modal therefore stays open with no user-visible feedback, since no error state exists in the component to display.
intelligence.fixApproach:
1. In the Add Task modal component, add a local error state (e.g. `const [error, setError] = useState(null)`). 2. In the submit handler, when the title is empty/whitespace, call `setError('Title is required')` and return without closing the modal or dispatching the create action. 3. Render the error message near the Title input (e.g. a `

` or inline text styled in red) and apply an error border class to the input when the error is set. 4. Clear the error whenever the user types in the title field, reopens the modal, or closes it. 5. Optionally add `required` and `autoFocus` to the title input as a first line of defence, and add a regression test asserting the error message appears after submitting with an empty title.

finding.title: All navigation routes except Board show the Project Board (My Tasks, Team, Reports, Sign In never render)
steps: Click 'My Tasks' in the header (URL changes to #tasks)
Repeat for 'Team', 'Reports', and load http://127.0.0.1:9902/#login directly
finding.expected: Each nav link should display its own view: My Tasks, Team, Reports, and a Sign In form.
finding.actual: Only the Project Board view ever renders. Clicking each nav link updates the URL hash (to #tasks, #team, #reports) but the content stays "Project Board + Add Task + kanban columns". Even a fresh page load directly at http://127.0.0.1:9902/#login renders the Project Board instead of a sign-in form.
finding.observed: Verified three ways: (1) clicked link "My Tasks" by role/name — URL became #tasks, content unchanged after 1.5s wait; (2) clicked "Team" and "Reports" — same result; (3) opened a fresh tab directly at #login — the Project Board with kanban columns rendered instead of a login form. No console errors accompany this, so the router appears to always fall through to the board view.
finding.impact: 4 of the 5 navigation destinations are unreachable; users can never see their tasks, the team page, reports, or reach the login screen. On mobile (393px) the Sign In link is additionally pushed off-screen, so there is no way at all to reach sign-in.

intelligence.rootCause: The client-side hash router always falls through to its default route (Project Board). Because even a direct load of #login renders the board, both the initial route resolution and the hashchange handling are failing - most likely the route table keys don't match the parsed hash (e.g., comparing 'tasks' against '#tasks', or missing/typo'd route entries), so the render switch always hits its default branch.
intelligence.fixApproach: 1. Inspect the router/bootstrap code (e.g., router.js or app init) and log the raw location.hash value being matched. 2. Normalize the hash before matching: strip the leading '#', trim, and lowercase (e.g., location.hash.replace(/^#/, '')). 3. Verify the route map/switch cases exactly match the hrefs in the header links ('tasks', 'team', 'reports', 'login') and that each maps to a distinct view render function. 4. Ensure the router runs once on DOMContentLoaded (initial load) and also subscribes to window 'hashchange'. 5. Make the render function fully replace the view container content per route, keeping the board only as an explicit fallback, then manually verify #tasks, #team, #reports and #login on both link clicks and direct loads.

finding.title: Header overflows viewport on mobile: 'Sign In' link is cut off and unclickable at 393px
finding.expected: All header links fit within the mobile viewport, ideally via a responsive/wrapping or collapsing nav (hamburger menu).
finding.actual: The Sign In link's bounding box is x=398..428 at a 393px viewport — entirely off the right edge. The header does not wrap and the page cannot scroll horizontally to it (attempted horizontal scroll; positions unchanged). A Playwright-style click on the link times out because it is not visible.
finding.observed: Snapshot geometry: Sign In anchor at x=398.16, width 30.55 in a 393px viewport. Nav links are laid out in one row (Board x=149, My Tasks x=210, Team x=267, Reports x=324, Sign In x=398) with no wrapping. browser_click by role/name timed out: 'element may be hidden or not yet rendered'.
finding.impact: On an iPhone-class device the authentication entry point is invisible and unreachable; combined with the routing defect, users cannot sign in at all on mobile.

intelligence.rootCause: The header navigation is rendered as a single non-wrapping flex/inline row (likely `flex-wrap: nowrap` or fixed-width items) whose combined width exceeds the 393px viewport, pushing the 'Sign In' link (x=398..428) entirely off-screen. Because the header overflows without triggering horizontal scroll or wrapping, the element is effectively unreachable and unclickable on mobile.
intelligence.fixApproach: 1. Inspect the header container's CSS and add `flex-wrap: wrap` and `max-width: 100%` as an immediate safeguard. 2. Implement a proper responsive pattern: add a media query (e.g. `@media (max-width: 480px)`) that hides the inline nav links and renders a hamburger/toggle menu, or stacks the nav vertically. 3. Verify link hit areas remain >=44px tap targets in the collapsed state. 4. Add a regression test that loads the page at 393px and asserts all header links have `boundingBox.x + width <= viewport.width` and are clickable.

finding.title: Task changes are lost on reload: created tasks and status moves reset to seed data
steps: Tap '+ Add Task', enter a title, tap 'Create' — the task appears in To Do
finding.expected: Created tasks and status changes should survive a page reload (via backend API or local storage).
finding.actual: The board resets to the initial five seeded tasks. The task created during testing ("QA smoke task") disappeared, and a task moved from To Do to In Progress ("Write documentation") was back in To Do after reload. The app issues no network requests other than the initial document GET, so state lives only in JS memory.
finding.observed: Sequence: added "QA smoke task" (To Do showed 3), clicked "Write documentation" card (moved to In Progress, To Do showed 1). After reloading http://127.0.0.1:9902/, board shows To Do (2) with "Write documentation" back in it and no "QA smoke task". Network log shows only the document GET; no state-saving API calls exist.
finding.impact: Any task a user adds or advances is silently discarded when the page is refreshed or reopened. For a project management tool, users lose their work with no warning.

intelligence.rootCause: Task state is held only in client-side JavaScript memory (component state seeded from a hardcoded array on mount). The 'Create Task' and status-change handlers mutate this in-memory array without any persistence call — the app makes zero network requests beyond the initial document GET and never writes to localStorage — so every reload re-initializes the seed data.
intelligence.fixApproach: 1) Choose a persistence layer: minimal fix is localStorage; robust fix is REST API endpoints (GET/POST/PATCH /api/tasks). 2) Replace hardcoded seed initialization with a load-from-store step that falls back to seeds only when the store is empty (first run). 3) In the create-task handler, persist the new task after updating state (POST to API or localStorage.setItem with the serialized list). 4) In the status-change/drag-drop handler, persist the updated task (PATCH /tasks/:id or resync localStorage). 5) Optionally centralize state in a store with a subscribe/effect that auto-syncs all mutations to the chosen backend, and add error handling for failed writes. 6) Verify by creating a task, moving another across columns, and reloading — both changes must survive.

ux.issue: Add Task modal silently no-ops when Title is empty: modal stays open, no task created, no validation message or field highlight anywhere on the page.
ux.impact: Users cannot tell why submission failed; they may retry repeatedly or assume the app is broken, eroding trust in the core task-creation flow.
ux.recommendation: Add inline validation on submit: show an error message (e.g. 'Title is required') adjacent to the field, mark the input with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, apply a visual error state, and set focus to the offending field. Optionally use the native required attribute as a baseline.

ux.issue: Navigation links change the URL hash but the visible content never changes, so 4 of 5 nav destinations (My Tasks, Team, Reports, Sign In) are dead ends that re-render the Project Board.
ux.impact: The app appears fundamentally broken; users cannot reach any feature beyond the board, and deep links like /#login fail on fresh load.
ux.recommendation: Treat as a functional routing defect, but also add user feedback while fixing: active-link state on the current route, graceful handling of unknown hashes, and a default route so the URL always matches the rendered view.

accessibility.issue: At a 393px viewport the Sign In link's bounding box (x=398..428) sits entirely outside the viewport, and the header neither wraps nor allows horizontal scroll.
accessibility.impact: The link is unreachable by pointer users, and keyboard users focusing it get no visible indication of where focus is, failing focus-visibility expectations.
accessibility.recommendation: Implement a responsive collapsing nav (hamburger) at small breakpoints, or allow header wrapping. Ensure any focused interactive element is always brought into view (scroll-into-view on focus) and remains visible.

patterns.pattern: Hash routing that mutates location.hash without a router bound to view rendering (no hashchange listener or initial-route resolution; every route falls through to the Project Board view).
patterns.recommendation: Introduce a minimal router: map '#/tasks', '#/team', '#/reports', '#/login' to view render functions, listen for hashchange, resolve the route on initial load, and render a default/fallback view for unmatched hashes.

patterns.pattern: All application state held only in JS memory with no persistence layer (zero network calls beyond the initial document GET; no localStorage usage), so mutations are discarded on reload.
patterns.recommendation: Persist mutations through a backend API (preferred, also enables multi-user features like Team) or localStorage as a fallback. Hydrate board state from the persistence layer on init instead of reseeding every load.

inventory.reportSummary: Audited TaskBoard (http://127.0.0.1:9902/) at iPhone 15 size (393×852) with a desktop cross-check. The board itself renders and core interactions work: the kanban shows 4 columns with seeded tasks, the Add Task modal opens, a task with a title is created successfully, Cancel dismisses, and clicking a task card advances it to the next column. However, navigation is fundamentally broken: My Tasks, Team, Reports, and Sign In routes all render the Project Board regardless of whether the link is clicked or the URL is loaded directly, so 4 of 5 destinations (including authentication) are unreachable. On mobile the header also overflows, pushing the Sign In link entirely off-screen. Add Task gives no feedback on empty submit, and all task changes are lost on reload (in-memory state only). No console errors or failed network requests were observed. Verdict: pass with issues — the board flow functions, but routing, mobile navigation access, validation feedback, and persistence need fixing before release.

findings.title: Add Task form gives no feedback when submitted with an empty title
findings.expected: Submitting the New Task form with an empty Title should show a visible validation error (e.g. "Title is required") explaining why the task was not created.
findings.actual: The modal stays open, no task is created, and no validation message, error text, or field highlight appears anywhere on the page (confirmed in both full-page text and screenshots). The form simply does nothing.
findings.observed: DOM bodyText after empty Create contains no error strings; screenshots of the modal show no message. A second empty submit after scrolling confirmed the same. Task count stayed at To Do (3).
findings.impact: Users who tap Create without typing a title get zero feedback and may believe the app is broken. Basic form usability/validation feedback is missing.

findings.title: All navigation routes except Board show the Project Board (My Tasks, Team, Reports, Sign In never render)
steps: Click 'My Tasks' in the header (URL changes to #tasks)
Repeat for 'Team', 'Reports', and load http://127.0.0.1:9902/#login directly
findings.expected: Each nav link should display its own view: My Tasks, Team, Reports, and a Sign In form.
findings.actual: Only the Project Board view ever renders. Clicking each nav link updates the URL hash (to #tasks, #team, #reports) but the content stays "Project Board + Add Task + kanban columns". Even a fresh page load directly at http://127.0.0.1:9902/#login renders the Project Board instead of a sign-in form.
findings.observed: Verified three ways: (1) clicked link "My Tasks" by role/name — URL became #tasks, content unchanged after 1.5s wait; (2) clicked "Team" and "Reports" — same result; (3) opened a fresh tab directly at #login — the Project Board with kanban columns rendered instead of a login form. No console errors accompany this, so the router appears to always fall through to the board view.
findings.impact: 4 of the 5 navigation destinations are unreachable; users can never see their tasks, the team page, reports, or reach the login screen. On mobile (393px) the Sign In link is additionally pushed off-screen, so there is no way at all to reach sign-in.

findings.title: Header overflows viewport on mobile: 'Sign In' link is cut off and unclickable at 393px
findings.expected: All header links fit within the mobile viewport, ideally via a responsive/wrapping or collapsing nav (hamburger menu).
findings.actual: The Sign In link's bounding box is x=398..428 at a 393px viewport — entirely off the right edge. The header does not wrap and the page cannot scroll horizontally to it (attempted horizontal scroll; positions unchanged). A Playwright-style click on the link times out because it is not visible.
findings.observed: Snapshot geometry: Sign In anchor at x=398.16, width 30.55 in a 393px viewport. Nav links are laid out in one row (Board x=149, My Tasks x=210, Team x=267, Reports x=324, Sign In x=398) with no wrapping. browser_click by role/name timed out: 'element may be hidden or not yet rendered'.
findings.impact: On an iPhone-class device the authentication entry point is invisible and unreachable; combined with the routing defect, users cannot sign in at all on mobile.

findings.title: Task changes are lost on reload: created tasks and status moves reset to seed data
steps: Tap '+ Add Task', enter a title, tap 'Create' — the task appears in To Do
findings.expected: Created tasks and status changes should survive a page reload (via backend API or local storage).
findings.actual: The board resets to the initial five seeded tasks. The task created during testing ("QA smoke task") disappeared, and a task moved from To Do to In Progress ("Write documentation") was back in To Do after reload. The app issues no network requests other than the initial document GET, so state lives only in JS memory.
findings.observed: Sequence: added "QA smoke task" (To Do showed 3), clicked "Write documentation" card (moved to In Progress, To Do showed 1). After reloading http://127.0.0.1:9902/, board shows To Do (2) with "Write documentation" back in it and no "QA smoke task". Network log shows only the document GET; no state-saving API calls exist.
findings.impact: Any task a user adds or advances is silently discarded when the page is refreshed or reopened. For a project management tool, users lose their work with no warning.
